Application Materials.content:
For PGT courses, you’ll provide a personal statement. It should share your motivation and enthusiasm for your chosen course and show your suitability for postgraduate study. Your statement should include examples of relevant work, voluntary or study experiences, and incorporate skills such as time management, project management, communication, teamwork, and problem-solving. You should also cover successes and achievements relevant to the course, outline why you have chosen the course and Newcastle University, and explain how you will apply your current skills, knowledge and experience. You may also consider showing how the course fits into your career plans and ambitions.
You’ll need to include contact details for **two referees**. At least one referee should be able to comment on your academic ability. Newcastle will contact your referees to request references, usually at the same time as sending the conditional offer. If you already have a reference, you can attach it in the application portal; the reference must be **signed by your referee, dated and on official letterhead**.
Check the “How to Apply” tab on your course page to see what documents to include. The main documents the University requires for postgraduate programmes are:
- A transcript of your degree studies; if you are still studying, provide a current transcript of your degree studies to date.
- Certificates to confirm your degree or highest qualification, if your degree is complete.
- Evidence of your English language ability.
- A copy of your passport.
- A curriculum vitae.
- A Personal Statement.
- Any transcripts of marks or certified documents should be translated into English.
Before submitting your application, you must attach a copy of any mandatory documents including your degree transcript. When uploading documents, select “Supporting Documentation,” click “Upload Documents,” select the document type from the dropdown list, choose files, and click “Submit.” For transcripts, select whether the document is a “transcript” or a “translated transcript.”

Interview Requirements.content: **All International students:** If you are an international student or a student from the EU, EEA or Switzerland and you need a visa to study in the UK, you must pay a deposit or submit an official letter of sponsorship. You may also be subject to academic and English language qualification verification, confirmation of funds and credibility interviews.

Application Deadlines.content:
**Start Dates:** The course starts in **September**.
**Closing Dates:** There is **no application closing date** for this course. We suggest international students apply **at least two months before the course starts**.

Academic Requirements.content:
A **2:2 honours degree, or international equivalent**. Your transcripts need to show an understanding of:
- **basic calculus**
- **probability theory**
- **statistical inference**
You can use your personal statement to show your mathematical knowledge if it is not clear from your transcripts.
For applicants from China: Students with a **4-year bachelor's degree from a recognised Chinese university** may be considered for entry onto a postgraduate course. Newcastle will assess applications using a **4 tier system**; requirements vary by course and depend on which tier your university belongs to.
| Entry Requirement | Tier 1 and 2 University | Tier 3 and 4 University |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2.2 | **70%** | **75%** |

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- **IELTS:** **6.5 overall** with a minimum of **6.0 in all sub-skills**.
- **Pearsons:** **70 overall** with a minimum of **65 in all sub-skills**.
- **Duolingo English Test:** **125 overall** with a minimum of **110 in Listening**, **115 in Reading**, **115 in Speaking**, and **125 in Writing** sub-skills.
- **TOEFL IBT or TOEFL IBT Special Home Edition prior to 21 January 2026:** **90 overall** with a minimum of **19 in Listening**, **20 in Reading**, **22 in Speaking**, and **20 in Writing** for sub-skills.
- **TOEFL IBT or TOEFL IBT Special Home Edition after 21 January 2026:** **4.5 overall** with a minimum of **3.5 in Reading**, **3.5 in Listening**, **3.5 in Speaking**, and **4 in Writing** for sub-skills.
- If you have lower English Language scores, you may be accepted onto a Pre-sessional English course.
- **PSE 6 weeks:** **IELTS 6.0 overall** with a minimum **5.5 in all sub-skills**. You can study the Pre-sessional English course at the Newcastle University International Study Centre.
- **PSE 10 weeks:** **IELTS 5.5 overall** with a minimum of **5.5 in all sub-skills**. You can study the Pre-sessional English course at the Newcastle University International Study Centre.
- Newcastle often accepts a wide range of English language tests and qualifications; applicants are directed to the English Language requirements web pages for more information and may contact the International Recruitment Team with queries.
- International students may be subject to academic and English language qualification verification, confirmation of funds and credibility interviews.

Program Overview.content:
Develop your career in the financial services, or as an analyst in investment banking and risk management fields. The financial services sector has grown worldwide, fuelling demand for suitably qualified graduates. With the Financial Analytics and Risk Management MSc, you will be ready to meet this demand. This programme strengthens your understanding of generalist finance issues and develops specialist practical skills in financial analytics and risk management. As a graduate, you'll be able to develop a career in the financial services sector. The course is also suitable for future analysts in economics and finance. This programme is delivered by the [Finance subject group](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/business/about/subject-groups/finance/).
The course provides the opportunity to develop relevant skills and a practical understanding of:
- the operation and behaviour of international financial markets
- the ability to analyse the strategies of financial market investors
- the role of finance in a modern economy
The course is modular. Depending on your modules, you'll be assessed through a combination of dissertation, essay, PC examination, portfolio, problem-solving exercises, report, written examination, and written exercise. Throughout your studies, you’ll have access to support from academic staff, academic advisers and research supervisors, the University Student Services Team, student representatives, and peers. You'll also be assigned an academic member of staff, who will be your academic adviser throughout your time with us.
Newcastle University Business School is accredited by the [Association to Advance Collegiate Schools of Business (AACSB)](http://www.aacsb.edu/), [European Quality Improvement System (EQUIS)](https://efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/), and [Association of MBAs (AMBA)](https://www.associationofmbas.com/about-us/). Only **1% of business schools worldwide** hold this triple crown. Newcastle University Business School is also recognised as an Academic Partner of the CQF Institute, the awarding body for the Certificate in Quantitative Finance (CQF). All students studying at the Business School are eligible to access member benefits.
You'll benefit from Newcastle University Business School’s status as a Bloomberg Experiential Learning Partner. Through self-study, you'll complete the Bloomberg Market Concepts certificate, which gives you an interactive introduction to the financial markets. You can take part in a live financial trading simulation delivered by a leading global provider of finance simulations, gaining insights into different roles in the financial industry and boosting your employability. You will get the chance to showcase your skills on the trading floor. You can also attend guest lectures that complement the study of theoretical frameworks and analyse recent trends in financial markets and banking industries.
Newcastle University Business School is an academic partner of the **CQF Institute**. You can register for free membership and access member-only benefits, including online technical talks and conferences, networking opportunities, career advice, thought leadership, and finance-focused introductory workshops.
The new Dual Award programme allows you to spend an additional academic year at Grenoble École de Management in Grenoble, France. After completing your postgraduate studies at Newcastle, you would join the last year of their Grande École programme, Masters in Management - M2 year. On successful completion, you will be awarded your Newcastle University degree and an MSc in Management from Grenoble. The Postgraduate Semester Abroad is an opportunity to study a complementary subject for one semester at a European partner university at the end of your studies, once you have submitted your dissertation/final project.

Graduates from this course will be able to undertake various roles, including financial trader, financial analyst, risk analyst, engineer on economic modelling, investor relations adviser, economist, and auditor. This course prepares you for a wide range of careers with employers such as HSBC Bank, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Normura, Tiburon Partners LLP, PwC, KPMG, and State Oil Company of Azerbaijan Republic.
Career development and employability are woven throughout teaching, learning and student experience. The School has dedicated employability support and career spaces to support you during your studies and for up to three years after graduation. Business School students get access to both the wider University careers service and exclusive Business School events and resources, including one-to-one career support, industry-specific career events, online career learning tools, career planning and information sessions, an annual careers week, networking opportunities, specialist careers and business start-up support, and the chance to apply for various work experience opportunities while studying.
Newcastle University Business School has over 4,000 students from over 85 countries. Its community includes regional, national and international leaders, over 37,000 alumni in 152 countries, leading professionals and academics, and businesses and partners in academia. The Business School is the gateway to [Newcastle Helix](https://newcastlehelix.com/home), a landmark 24 acre hybrid city quarter. Facilities include computer clusters, lecture theatres, seminar and teaching spaces, a dedicated Student Hub and Quiet Space, employability support and event hubs, a Bloomberg lab with over 20 terminals, and the Experimental and Behavioural Economics Lab.

Curriculum.content:
The course is modular. **Full time: 12 months**. The course starts in September.
This course will provide the opportunity for you to develop relevant skills and a practical understanding of:
- the operation and behaviour of international financial markets

Postgraduate Study Abroad options include:

Cost of Attendance.content:
Living costs cover expenses other than tuition fees, such as accommodation, food, drink, travel and study materials. The average cost of living for a student studying in the UK is just over **£1,100 per month**.
Estimated monthly costs while studying at Newcastle:
- Rent in University-owned or managed partnership accommodation, including bills such as electricity, water, gas and wifi: Postgraduate **£392 - £940**.
- Groceries: **£144**.
- Socialising: **£99**.
- Mobile phone (SIM only): **£16**.
- Course costs, which can include books, stationery, photocopying, field trips, and specialist materials or equipment: estimated at around **£11 - £59** per month.
For international students, visa applications require proof of sufficient funds to support yourself while at university in the UK. International students will also have further costs associated with studying in the UK, such as a student visa and a health surcharge to access the NHS.

Financial Aid.content:
**You may be eligible for a scholarship worth 25% off the international fee**. [Search our funding database](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/postgraduate/fees-funding/).
Newcastle supports EU and international students by providing a range of Vice-Chancellor's automatic and merit-based scholarships. See the [searchable postgraduate funding page](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/postgraduate/fees-funding/search-funding/) for more information.
Find funding available for your course through the course funding and scholarships search.
If you're applying for funding, always check the funding application deadline. This deadline may be earlier than the application deadline for your course. For some funding schemes, you need to have received an offer of a place on a course before you can apply for the funding.

Multiple Applications.content: You may have received multiple programme offers, but please note that you can only accept one. Once you confirm your acceptance, all other offers—including applications still awaiting decisions—will be automatically declined. However, if you change your mind, you can request to reinstate a previously declined offer, subject to availability.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: If you decide to defer your offer, log in to the application portal you applied through to let us know. For most courses, you can defer your offer to the next academic year. If we’re able to defer your offer and you have a deposit condition outstanding, we’ll apply a January deposit condition for the following year. We’ll decline your current offer and send you a new offer for the next academic year. If we are unable to defer your offer, we’ll ask you to apply again the following year. You can only defer your offer once. To defer for a further year, you’ll need to submit a new application the following year.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
There are two types of offer: unconditional and conditional.
- **Conditional offer:** “You’ll receive a conditional offer if there are conditions that you need to meet before you can start your course.” The conditions are in the “Terms and Conditions of your Offer” section of the offer document and can also be viewed in the application portal.
- To evidence that conditions have been met, applicants must upload supporting documents to the application portal. If still studying, upload documents as soon as they are available. If supporting documents are not in English, certified English language translations must be provided.
- “When your documents demonstrate that you’ve met your offer conditions, your offer will become unconditional.” If an applicant has “just missed the conditions” of the offer, they are encouraged to upload results anyway; Newcastle will review the application and “may still be able to give you a place on your chosen course.”
- Types of condition include academic conditions, such as “a transcript of your degree studies” and “your degree certificate or a certified copy”; references; and English language conditions.
- English language conditions can be met by taking an [international language test](https://www.ncl.ac.uk/international/language/#overview) such as IELTS, TOEFL, or Pearsons, or by completing one of Newcastle’s six- or ten-week English language courses at the [International Study Centre](https://nclisc.com/en/courses/pre-sessional-english).
- When applicants have accepted the offer and met any conditions, Newcastle sends a Confirmation of a Place (COP), which is “formal confirmation of your acceptance of the unconditional offer.”
